selected.hook_line: If you grew as big as an elephant, could your legs still hold your weight?
selected.viewer_expectation: A giant human would simply be bigger, stronger, and able to walk normally.
selected.visible_contradiction: Weight grows with volume, but bone strength only grows with cross-section area.
selected.frame_zero: A scaled model leg built with human proportions snaps under four tons of simulated weight.
selected.character_action: The scholar gently places a proportional torso load onto a scaled human leg frame.
selected.reaction: A quiet blink of surprise followed by a gentle tap on the cracked support timber.
selected.activity: Testing how scaling height without widening bone width breaks upright support.
selected.location: An outdoor comparative anatomy pavilion beside full-size animal leg casts.
selected.topic_link: Body mass increases much faster than the cross-section area of supporting bones.
selected.factual_anchor: A human scaled to the size and weight of an elephant, where volume grows faster than bone area.
selected.payoff: An elephant-sized human would collapse because normal human leg proportions cannot carry four tons.

entry_bridge.a_end: The scholar rests his palm on an embossed topic book resting on a stone display pedestal.
entry_bridge.b_start: Top-down view of the closed book bound in rough hide-textured leather on the pedestal.
entry_bridge.reveal: The book opens to an illustrated comparison of slender human legs versus elephant pillars.
entry_bridge.world_entry: A four-ton giant human figure collapses onto its knees as slender leg bones buckle under the body.

novelty.prop_family: scaled leg bone model and weighted torso block
novelty.reveal_family: bone area falls behind total volume growth
